## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

*Lokuttarakusala* ("Supramundane Wholesome", Ds 2.1.5) is a major analytical section within the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī*, the first book of the Pali Abhidhamma Piṭaka. In the systematic architecture of the text, following the initial tripartite division of dhammas outlined in the *mātikā*, wholesome phenomena (*kusala-dhammas*) are examined across different spheres of existence: the sense sphere (*kāmâvacara*), fine-material sphere (*rūpâvacara*), immaterial sphere (*arūpâvacara*), and the supramundane (*lokuttara*) [Gethin 2001]. In secondary reference literature and later manuals, the term *lokuttarakusala* is predominantly discussed doctrinally as the four transcendent path-consciousnesses (*magga-citta*) that directly eradicate defilements.
